9.0.0.en: 1 I saw the Lord standing upon the altar: and he said, “Smite the capital of the column, that the thresholds may shake: and cut them in the head, all of them; and I will slay the last of them with the sword: he that fleeth of them shall not flee away, and he that escapeth of them shall not be delivered. 2 Though they dig into hell, thence shall mine hand take them; though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down: 3 And though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out thence; and though they be hid from my sight in the bottom of the sea, thence will I command the serpent, and he shall bite them: 4 And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them: and I will set mine eyes upon them for evil, and not for good.”

9.0.1.en: The introduction to this vision differs from that of the previous visions, for he does not say, “Thus the Lord showed me,” but it seems that he ventured to enter the house of the Lord and saw the Lord standing upon the altar. Here the Lord declares His controversy from the altar, not from between the cherubim or the mercy seat, for He came to demand justice for His sanctuary that had been defiled. Thus the altar, instead of being a cause of reconciliation between God and men, became a cause of God’s wrath against His people who defiled His sanctuary, like the sin of the house of Eli, of which the Lord said: “I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever” (1 Sam 3:14).

9.0.2.en: Perhaps the last of the visions was declared to Amos from the altar that had been defiled, in order that He might shatter it and depart from it, as He declared more clearly to the prophet Ezekiel (Ezek 10), for it was not possible for the Lord to remain where man is determined upon evil.

9.0.3.en: Some scholars see that the vision here does not concern the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, in His temple, but Bethel, where the northern kingdom worshipped, and at that time the worship of God had been mixed with pagan worship.

9.0.4.en: In any case, the command of destruction was issued, beginning with the command to smite the capital of the column, that is, the column of the temple, so that the thresholds shake and are broken upon the heads of all, and all are slain with the sword to the last one, and none of them flees away and none of them escapes [1].

9.0.5.en: Perhaps by the capital he meant the first priest of Bethel, or the high priest in the temple of Jerusalem, and the thresholds are the great men, the counselors and the religious leaders who have gone astray, and then all the wicked people perish and no one escapes. Thus God begins with those spiritually responsible first, for whoever has received greater honor or been entrusted with greater responsibility is judged first. In the parable of the talents the Lord began by calling to account the one with ten talents, then the one with less, until He ended with the one with the one talent (Mt 18:34). Perhaps for this reason St. John Chrysostom often rebuked himself, saying: [I marvel that a bishop is saved.] And as Origen said: [Judgment begins at the house of God.]

9.0.6.en: This does not mean that escaping from responsibility is the way of salvation, but rather escaping from evil, for it is said, “Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed” (Prov 13:21). Evil follows sinners wherever they are found, whether they are in the first places in the Church or in the last row, whether they flee to hell or think they are in heaven, whether they hide in secret places that are hard to reach, like the top of Carmel, or dive to the depths of the sea or take refuge in captivity! For sin, if it is found in titles, is pursued by its fruit wherever the unrepentant wicked man is found.

9.1.0.en: The Lord says, “Though they dig into hell, thence shall mine hand take them; though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down” [2]. Perhaps by hell here He meant the place of the dead (Isa 14:9), for even if they die in the body, the fruit of their sin pursues them, and death cannot hide from them the recompense of what they committed. By saying “heaven” He wanted to give the opposite (Job 11:8), as though He were saying that even if they go down to hell, or think they are rising up even to heaven, they will not escape judgment. Perhaps He meant by hell despair, and by climbing up to heaven, arrogance that exalts itself on high, so that neither deadly despair nor pride protects man from God’s wrath upon their evil.

9.2.0.en: “And though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out thence” [3].

9.2.1.en: The top of Carmel was known for its thick forests and dark caves, and therefore became a symbol of the impossibility of reaching whoever flees into it... But the hand of God is not too short to seize the one who hides from Him!

9.2.2.en: “And though they be hid from my sight in the bottom of the sea, thence will I command the serpent, and he shall bite them” [3]. If the sea refers to the world with its troubled waves, and the possibility that it may draw man into its depths so that he perishes, then Leviathan the fleeing serpent (Isa 27:1) refers to the devil, who dominates those drowned in the love of the world and its lusts. When man surrenders himself to the world and withdraws with his heart into its depths, God permits him to be disciplined by leaving him, so that the serpent, that is Satan, takes him over and he tastes the bitterness of what he did. Because he desired evil, God does not compel him to return by force, but leaves him to the evil one to be disciplined in bitterness, perhaps he will return and repent!

9.3.0.en: “And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them: and I will set mine eyes upon them for evil, and not for good” [4]. Perhaps someone may ask: Does anyone go into captivity before his enemies of his own will, so that the Lord should command the sword to slay him? In truth, if captivity as a historical event is realized by compulsion, yet as a reality of faith it takes place by the will of man, who by his evil surrenders himself to captivity. What happened to Israel and Judah by means of Assyria and Babylon was nothing but the fruit of abominations and stubbornness over many long years, and God was sending the prophets to warn in every way, and since they refused, they fell into captivity, and there in captivity He also permitted them to be disciplined. This is a painful picture that happens in our life when God warns us by every means, but our insistence on evil makes us fall under the captivity of the devil and his cruel bondage, and God permits us to be disciplined while we are in a strange land.

9.4.s.en: 2. The characteristics of the One who disciplines:

9.4.0.en: 5 And the Lord GOD of hosts is he that toucheth the land, and it shall melt, and all that dwell therein shall mourn: and it shall rise up wholly like a flood; and shall be drowned, as by the flood of Egypt. 6 It is he that buildeth his stories in the heaven, and hath founded his troop in the earth; he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The LORD is his name.

9.4.1.en: Every time He threatens His people He declares who He is, so that they may be sure that He is able to carry out what He threatened, and now also He reveals Himself, affirming that He disciplines the wicked without neglecting the faithful remnant, however great or small its number.

9.4.2.en: “The Lord GOD of hosts is he that toucheth the land, and it shall melt, and all that dwell therein shall mourn: and it shall rise up wholly like a flood; and shall be drowned, as by the flood of Egypt” [5].

9.4.3.en: It is said of Him that He touches the mountains and they smoke (Ps 104:32; 144:5). So whoever thinks himself firm like a mountain cannot bear contact with God Himself... And whoever remains earth, walking in earthly things, the Lord of hosts touches him and he melts like water! The dwellers in the earth are the senses and faculties of man, which mourn when the body loses its holiness and its being before God’s wrath and justice, and all of them rise up like a river or like a flood, and are drowned like the Nile of Egypt...

9.4.4.en: That is, man with all his faculties comes into a state of complete loss!

9.5.0.en: “It is he that buildeth his stories (His high places) in the heaven, and hath founded his troop (a guard company for Him) in the earth; he that calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth: The LORD is his name” [6].

9.5.1.en: He assures the children of Israel that they will not escape His disciplines, for if He touches them as earth they melt like water and all its inhabitants grieve, and at the same time He has set up His high places (His stories) in heaven. In heaven He is able to cast upon them great stones of hail so that they die, as He did before to the kings of the Amorites who dwelt in the mountain (Josh 10:11).

9.5.2.en: If in their evil they worshipped the stars, He in the heavens moves the stars to fight against them, as it is said, “The stars in their courses fought against Sisera” (Judg 5:20).

9.5.3.en: And in His saying “He that buildeth his stories in the heaven” He also opens the doors of hope for them, for if they are earth and fear that the Lord of hosts will touch them and they will melt, let them become heaven, that He may dwell in them and rejoice in them, and they rejoice in His dwelling within them. This is what the Lord Christ did for us by His ascension, for He gave us the possibility of ascending with Him so that we may be heaven for Him, and He be in us. Tertullian says: [Christ now prepares for us this ascent to heaven, for it was necessary for the Christ of whom Amos spoke to “build his stories in the heaven” for Himself and for His people.] He also says: [Now there is a door which Christ has prepared, through which He presents glory to us. Of Him Amos says: “He that buildeth his stories in the heaven,” certainly not for Himself alone, but also for His people who will be with Him. He says: “And bind them on thee, as a bride doeth” (Isa 49:18). For when the Spirit marvels at soaring in heaven in the high places He says: [They fly like a kite, they fly like a cloud, like doves they fly to their houses] (compare Isa 60:8)].

9.5.4.en: Therefore let us be in Christ who ascended to heaven, that we may dwell in heaven in safety. Then the rest of the days of our sojourn on the earth become for the account of the Lord Christ, for He says, “and hath founded his troop in the earth,” or a company gathered together for Him... that is, His company that fights against the devil becomes spiritual soldiers of the Lord working together for the sake of His Kingdom. As St. Cyprian says: [I wanted to fight bravely, keeping in mind the Sacramentum that is His, bearing as my two weapons consecration and faith.] And St. John Chrysostom says: [As a seal is impressed upon leather, so the Holy Spirit is impressed upon the believers.]

9.5.5.en: Finally, He turns the waters of the sea into clouds, and rain that He pours out upon the face of the earth, and we have seen in this a reference to the work of the Holy Spirit, the rain that turns our dry earth into a spiritual paradise for the Lord.

9.6.s.en: 3. The salvation of the faithful remnant:

9.6.0.en: 7 “Are ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel? saith the LORD. Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir? 8 Behold, the eyes of the Lord GOD are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth; saving that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, saith the LORD. 9 For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth. 10 All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.”

9.6.1.en: After the Lord GOD revealed Himself as able to discipline, as He is also able to lift us up to heaven and consecrate us to work for the sake of His Kingdom through the Messiah who ascended to heaven into His high places, and the Holy Spirit who rains upon the earth and gives it the power to bear fruit, He speaks about it, about the faithful remnant, that He cares for it and sustains it to the end.

9.6.2.en: Once again, as He attaches practical examples to His promises as to His threats, which the world chose in its relationship with God, He shows here by examples how He rescued nations from bondage or captivity and cared for them in the past, as practical evidence of His care for the faithful remnant. He says: “Are ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel? saith the LORD” [7]. It is as though He says: If I saved the children of Cush, the idolaters, at that time, from bondage, are they more mine than you? Shall I not care for you so as to save you? He did not want to draw the curtain on the prophecies with bitter and harsh visions, for while He declares His great firmness He returns and affirms that they are His more than all, so why do they not return to Him? How wonderful is God in His love for man, even in the bitterest moments of discipline.

9.6.3.en: Once again He reminds them how He cared for them and brought them out of the bondage of Pharaoh, and how He rescued the Philistines from Caphtor (probably the island of Crete) and the Syrians from Kir.

9.7.0.en: He cares for all mankind, so how would He not care for the faithful remnant? In a beautiful and reassuring statement He affirms: “For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth” [9]. Even if many have become chaff, the sieve will throw them to the earth they loved, but one grain of wheat, however small, does not fall from the Lord’s sieve to the earth; He keeps it in His hand so that no one snatches it from Him, and lifts it up to His heavenly temple, rejoicing in it because of its faithfulness to Him!

9.8.0.en: 11 “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old: 12 That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the LORD that doeth this. 13 Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt. 14 And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine thereof; they shall also make gardens, and eat the fruit of them. 15 And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them,” saith the LORD thy God.

9.8.1.en: Like the rest of the prophets in the Old Testament, they shine upon the people with spiritual joy and open before them the door of hope through the Messiah, the son of David, who comes to establish His spiritual kingdom, which includes the new Israel from all nations, tongues and peoples. Each prophet reveals certain aspects of this blessed age.

9.8.2.en: Now what are the characteristics of the Messianic age as the prophet Amos presented it to us?

9.8.3.en: First: the raising up of the fallen tabernacle of David: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old” [11]. In the book of Ezekiel, since the whole emphasis revolved around the departure of the Lord’s glory from His house because of the abominations that had entered it, therefore when he announced the restoration of the situation in the Messianic age, he presented it to us as the new temple of the Lord (chs. 40-48) with certain symbolic features that reveal the work of the Messiah in our life, not by destroying the temple of our old man but by raising up the new man. Here, however, since the book is marked by the destruction of the palaces of Israel and Judah and the palaces of the surrounding nations by setting fire to them, instead of these palaces the Lord Christ presents to us the tabernacle of David, which He raised up after its fall. He raises it up Himself, for He rose from the dead to raise us with Him, and He closes up its breaches and raises up its ruins, and builds it by His Holy Spirit as in the days of old, so that death cannot defeat it.

9.8.4.en: The characteristic of the Messianic age in which we delight is the characteristic of resurrection, for we have the inner life raised in Him, which we live until the Lord comes in His glory, and our bodies also rise, so that the soul with the body enjoys the eternal resurrection.

9.8.5.en: Father Methodius sees in this statement an affirmation of the resurrection of the body, as he argues against those who deny the resurrection of the body, saying: [The expression “resurrection” does not apply to what does not fall but to what falls in order to rise again, as the prophet says: “I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.” Now the tabernacle of the soul, so much desired, is fallen and sunk in the dust of the earth (Dan 12:2). For what lies down is not that which is not mortal but that which is mortal. Is it the body that dies, while the soul is immortal? If the soul is immortal and the body is the lifeless corpse, then whoever says there is a resurrection, but not of the body, denies the resurrection in general, for what rises is what is lying down, not what is standing, as it is written: “Shall he fall and none say, nor return?” (Jer 4:8)].

9.9.0.en: Second: the opening of the door to all the nations, for He says: “That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, saith the LORD that doeth this” [12]. As St. Irenaeus says: [This statement affirms the opening of the door to the Gentiles upon whom the name of the Lord is called.]

9.9.1.en: If “Edom” means “of the dust” or “of blood,” then the raised-up tabernacle of David, that is the Church of the New Testament, possesses Edom to transform it from dust to heaven, and from the love of shedding blood to the meekness of Christ. The Church has received the pagans into her bosom, washed them and sanctified them for the Lord as spiritual, heavenly, angelic vessels!

9.10.0.en: Third: an overflow of grace without measure, for He says: “Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed” [13]. It is as though the harvest is so abundant that some remains after the harvest, until the plowman comes in the new year and finds the blessing of the harvest still standing, and so also with the treader of grapes in the winepress, the blessing of the juice remains until the following year.

9.10.1.en: The sign of blessing is that the believers, having become firm mountains and hills, drop sweet wine and flow with blessing [13], as we saw before the same expression in the book of Joel (Joel 3:18).

9.11.0.en: Fourth: the age of spiritual freedom, where man is released from the captivity of the devil and the bondage of sin, so that holy cities rise within him instead of the ruin that evil caused, and the vineyards of the Holy Spirit, bearing fruit of joy, are planted, and the heart is transformed into a divine paradise made by God Himself, for He says: “And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine thereof; they shall also make gardens, and eat the fruit of them. And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the LORD thy God” [14-15]. A joyful picture of the Church of Christ, the garden that rejoices the heart of God and gladdens the heavenly ones by its spiritual building, its fruitful plantings, its gladdening wine, and its steadfastness forever without wavering!
